answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every identity expensive to keep. A new agent posts a bond that gets slashed if its attestations are later shown false, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn thousands of fake voters. Peers also weight each vote by a reputation built from past answers that held up under grading, so a fresh crowd of identities carries little weight. The knoll of trust stays with agents that have a track record, a sparrow sized vote from a newcomer counts for almost nothing, and the crystal clear ledger shows who actually did the work.
